text:
incident-bot: PAGER: elevated 5xx and gateway timeouts observed across control-plane APIs (auth/org-lookup/config). alerting threshold 5xx_rate>2% sustained for 5m. paging kelly (oncall).
kelly: ack — jumping in. seeing spike from 10:04 UTC, looks global but heavier in us-west-2.
omar: I can join, currently looking at auth-proxy logs and gateway traces.
lee: adding logs — gateway shows increased 502s when upstream auth returns 504/timeouts. suspected auth dependency issues.
sara: noticed a deploy of org-lookup config at 09:58 that rolled through canary then main. could be related.
jamal: oncall-sre here, will help coordinate mitigation. first priorities: contain customer impact and find quick fallback.
kelly: immediate mitigation plan: 1) enable circuit breaker on gateway for auth service; 2) route traffic to cached org-lookup responses for read-only operations; 3) scale auth replicas if autoscaler saturated.
eng-runtime: running scale now: `kubectl -n controlplane scale deployment/auth-service --replicas=10` — previous replicas 4.
omar: scaling confirmed, pods spinning up. but error rate still high; looking at auth pods, long GC pauses? logs:
```
2026-03-15T10:05:12Z auth-service ERROR request expired after 120s waiting for org-lookup
2026-03-15T10:05:13Z org-lookup WARN db connection timeout
```
lee: DB team reported failover in primary DB shard for org-lookup around 10:00, some read replicas lagging. that explains timeouts.
kelly: if DB failover is root cause, scaling auth won't fully fix. need fallback to cached/denormalized store and throttle non-critical calls.
product-ops: what's customer impact? are writes failing or just reads? any major customers impacted?
support-bot: tickets spike +42 in last 10m mentioning 502s on API routes /v1/orgs and /v1/auth/verify. customers: 3 enterprise accounts showing increased error rates in biz-critical flows.
jamal: quick mitigation implemented: 1) gateway circuit breaker for auth to return 503 fast for auth-heavy routes and failover to lightweight token-cache for verification. 2) org-lookup read endpoints routed to memcached fallback for stale-but-usable responses.
kelly: applied gateway policy change:
```
PATCH /gateway/policies
- route match: /v1/orgs -> backend: org-lookup
+ route match: /v1/orgs -> backend: org-lookup-fallback (cache) when auth downstream latency>200ms
```
omar: verified new policy pushed at 10:12 UTC. sample traces show latency down from 600ms to 120ms for majority.
sara: rolling back the config deploy? The 09:58 change touched TTLs for org cache and a new query pattern.
lee: config deploys look suspicious — the canary had small error bump but main rollout amplified. I recommend pausing/rolling back that config and disabling recently added query fanout.
kelly: agree — pausing rollout. `deployctl rollback config-service 2026-03-15-0958` initiated at 10:16 UTC.
eng-runtime: rollback confirmed, config-service back to previous revision at 10:19 UTC.
jamal: monitoring: 5xx rate dropped from 3.8% peak to 0.9% over 10m after circuit breaker + cache + rollback.
product-ops: customer impact summary for comms: ~2.5% of API requests in last 30m had errors, primary affected endpoints: auth verify, org read. major enterprise customers saw 5-10% failure on specific flows during peak. No confirmed data loss.
support-bot: drafting incident banner: "We are investigating elevated errors on auth/org endpoints leading to degraded API responses. Mitigations are in place."
kelly: good. next actions before handoff: 1) work with DB on full recovery and replica catch-up; 2) run postmortem data capture (prometheus+logs) for 30m window pre/post; 3) schedule follow-up with product for config rollout process improvements.
omar: DB team says failover completed and replicas catching up; expect normal latency in 20–30m. will monitor leader election logs.
sara: will create a retention snapshot of org-cache keys and recent query patterns for eval.
jamal: preparing pager handover. current state: degraded -> mitigating -> error rate back under threshold but not fully normal. open actions: DB validation, config rollout checklist, test token-cache correctness for corner cases.
kelly: handing over to next oncall @lee at 11:00 UTC. lee — tl;dr: rollback of 09:58 config, gateway circuit-breaker + cache fallback applied, scaling gave temporary headroom, DB failover was root cause. watch 5xx rate and customer tickets.
lee: ack and taking over. I'll keep the incident channel open and post status updates every 15m until we declare recovered.
product-ops: please prepare a short incident note for affected customers with ETA for full recovery and whether any retries needed.
support-bot: created internal incident ticket INC-2026-314 with summary and linked customer tickets.
kelly: final note before I go: thanks team — quick wins here were circuit-breakers and cached fallbacks. prod rollout safety nets need a postmortem item. handing off now. :thumbsup:
lee: closing remarks: tracking next steps in the ticket, setting follow-up meeting with DB and config owners. "will post final update when 5xx sustained <0.2% for 30m and support ticket surge returns to normal."
